stages.journal: Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers asked me to end Rows-For-Another's Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate: eleven years for one holed boat. She gave me a leaf in her own hand to leave in the count-box for the real one, five lockpicks, and 100 gold, the Owing's first price. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the farm.

Rows-For-Another told me what holds her: her leaf in the count-box inside the estate house, whose key the keeper Hulm-Tei wears; Hulm-Tei's word, which could close the Owing; and Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel north of the bank, who knows the way to her home tree. I'm to break any one of the three.

I took Rows-For-Another's leaf from the count-box and left Never-Sold's in its place. Under it lay the keeper's own leaf, with Hulm-Tei's name on it: whatever any leaf comes up short is written onto his. If I hand hers in, her eleven years fall on him. I'm to bring hers to Never-Sold, or give Hulm-Tei back his own.

I talked Brings-Them-Back round. He will look the other way when Rows-For-Another goes by the channel, but he still knows the way to her home tree. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.

I paid Brings-Them-Back 150 gold, his head-price. He will look the other way when Rows-For-Another goes by the channel, but he still knows the way to her home tree. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.

I killed Brings-Them-Back where the channel runs on north of the bank. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now, to fetch her back from it. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
I talked Hulm-Tei round. He took the first price, struck Rows-For-Another's leaf and wrote her eleven years onto his own, knowing what he did. I'm to tell Never-Sold.

I gave Hulm-Tei back his own leaf with the first price. He struck Rows-For-Another's leaf and said the damp had taken his. He leaves the estate at the reckoning, and what she owed will be shared among the hands who stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
I paid Hulm-Tei the whole of what Rows-For-Another's leaf had grown to, 1,000 gold. He struck her leaf, and nobody carries anything for it. I'm to tell Never-Sold.

I gave Never-Sold Rows-For-Another's leaf, and she will read it aloud and burn it. Rows-For-Another is free; her eleven years fall on Hulm-Tei's leaf, or on every hand of the estate if his leaf is gone too. Never-Sold paid me, named me one of the Chainbreakers and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Hulm-Tei struck Rows-For-Another's leaf with his own hand. She is free, and what it cost fell where his word put it. Never-Sold paid me, named me one of the Chainbreakers and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Her Owing was never closed: it will be written onto the keeper, and the fetcher still knows the way to her home tree, so she can never go back to it. Never-Sold paid me half, named me one of the Chainbreakers and said to come back to her for more work.

I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home, and her Owing will be written onto the keeper. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.

I gave Never-Sold Rows-For-Another's leaf, which I had taken from the estate's count-box before she asked me. She will read it aloud and burn it, and the eleven years fall on the estate's keeper. Never-Sold paid me, named me one of the Chainbreakers and said to come back to her for more work.
Never-Sold or Rows-For-Another is dead. The Owing cannot be ended now.

refs.name: Rows-For-Another's Leaf
refs.text: Rows-For-Another, boat-hand. Holed the second boat off the bank: four nushmeekos. [The next lines are in a small, exact hand.] First year: bread, roof, net and the boat's upkeep, eleven; worked, six. A fever in the rains: one more. Second year: the same. [From the third year the hand is larger, and the same line runs on for nine years more.] Owed at the last reckoning: sixty nushmeekos.

refs.name: The Keeper's Leaf
refs.text: Hulm-Tei, hatched owing on this ground. What any leaf is short at the reckoning is written here. If this leaf is lost, the shortfall is shared among all. Under it, eleven shortfalls in his own hand: a runaway's two seasons, a drowned hand's four, a boat lost, a fever's months; none of them Rows-For-Another's.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.chainbreaker-patron
lines.prompt: What is an Owing?
lines.text: There are no jails in Black Marsh. When a person does a wrong, they pay it in work, in nushmeekos. A nushmeeko is one month of work that nobody thanks you for, and once it is worked off nobody mentions it again. In the south that has gone bad. Whoever holds the estate or the landing does the reckoning, and he writes food, breakage and sickness onto the months until they never end. A person can be born owing and die owing. I was born owing, and I got out. That is why I do what I do.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.chainbreaker-patron
lines.prompt: Why do the held go grey?
lines.text: The Hist is the tree a tribe is hatched under. Our colour comes from it, and so does the way home when we die. A person held for years far from their Hist loses that colour. It fades, and they go grey. Rows-For-Another has been eleven years away from hers. She is afraid of going grey, and she is right to be.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.chainbreaker-patron
lines.prompt: Who are the Chainbreakers?
lines.text: We are a few dozen, in Blackrose and round it, and we get the held out. Our oath is three words. Bones go home. An Owing stands on three legs. The first is the count, which the holder keeps under lock. The second is the word that says it stands. The third is the hand, someone paid to fetch a runaway back. Take one leg away and the whole Owing falls. We take them with a key lifted off a belt, a lock opened in the dark, a keeper faced down at his own door and a fetcher met on a channel bank. Nobody else is going to do it.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.chainbreaker-patron
lines.prompt: What does the Chainbreakers' work pay, and why might I not want it?
lines.text: It pays a thief's share in coin, and picks from my own store. Understand what you would be. A Chainbreaker caught at a holder's box is a thief under the marsh's law, and the sentence for a thief is an Owing of their own. So you would be owing, as the people we free are owing. Think on that before you say yes. If you would rather not, walk away. It costs you nothing.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.chainbreaker-patron
lines.prompt: What is the job?
lines.text: Her name is Rows-For-Another. Eleven years ago she holed a boat on the Tulm-Varo estate north of town, and the estate's keeper set her four nushmeekos, four months of work. She owes more now than she did then. I give you a leaf in my own hand, five picks and 100 gold. Her leaf lies in the estate's count-box: take it, and leave mine in its place. The gold is the first price. By custom an Owing paid at its first price is closed for good, and Hulm-Tei, the keeper, has refused it from me twice. He may not refuse it from someone who brings more than coin. There are three doors, and any one will do: rob the box, make Hulm-Tei strike her leaf himself, or get past Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel. Each door costs. Seen at the box, you are a thief on the estate's ground. Kill the fetcher and you have a death on you. Go north past the farm with its cattle and its big house, to the channel bank beyond. Hear from Rows-For-Another how she is held.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.chainbreaker-patron
lines.prompt: I already have Rows-For-Another's leaf. I took it from the estate's count-box.
lines.text: Then you have run ahead of me, and the work is done. Give it here. Tonight I read every line of it aloud and burn it. Rows-For-Another's four months and the eleven years after them end in that fire. A leaf does not leave a box for nothing. Someone on that farm will answer for it, and I will not say who tonight. I pay you for it, and you are one of the Chainbreakers now. Bones go home.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.chainbreaker-patron
lines.prompt: Tell me the job again.
lines.text: Rows-For-Another's Owing is to be ended, by the count-box, by Hulm-Tei's word or by the channel. Whichever you have done, come to me with her leaf if you hold it, or with word that she is free or gone. The estate house is the big house on the farm north of the town, by the cattle. Hulm-Tei stands inside it. Brings-Them-Back stands where the channel runs on north of the bank, and Rows-For-Another stands on the bank itself. Back south past the farm to my house when you have news.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.estate-debtor
lines.prompt: Who are you?
lines.text: I am Rows-For-Another, who was a boat-hand of the Tulm-Varo, and I wait on this bank. A boat I holed put me in an Owing, which is the work a debt sets on you, and that was eleven years ago. I do not ask strangers for anything. I will say that I have not stood under my Hist, the tree I was hatched under, in all those years, and I am afraid of going grey before I do. The big house on the farm south of this bank is the estate house, and its keeper stands inside it, by the cattle. The man who fetches runaways keeps to the channel where it runs on north of here. If you want the rest, go back south past the farm to the Chainbreakers' house on the town's north side. The woman who keeps it can tell you my debt.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.estate-debtor
lines.prompt: Never-Sold sent me. Tell me how you are held.
lines.text: I holed a Tulm-Varo boat eleven years ago, and the Owing for it, the work I must do to pay, is not ended yet. The tree my tribe is hatched under is the Hist, and I have not stood under mine in all that time. Look at my arms. My colour is still mine, but every morning I look for the day it fades, and I think of walking home grey, with my own kin asking whose child I am. Three things hold me. The keeper, Hulm-Tei, stands in the big house on the farm by the cattle and carries the key to the count-box in it, where my leaf lies, the page that says what I owe. His word is the second: by custom he may take the first price and close an Owing for good, and he has refused it. The third is Brings-Them-Back. He fetches runaways on this channel for a head-price, and he stands where it runs on north of this bank. He knows the way to my tree, so if I run while he lives, I can never go home. Each way out has its cost, as far as I know it. Lift my leaf from the box and my Owing goes with it. What that costs the keeper I cannot say. Ask for his word and you must move him, and he will tell you every line on my leaf is true: four months, then my food, then a fever. He is right. It has outgrown me. The channel costs most: buy the fetcher and he looks away, yet still knows my tree; kill him and I may go home, with a man dead for my sake. That is why I want my Owing closed, not fled. When the channel is clear, because he is dead or has agreed to look away, come and tell me.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.estate-debtor
lines.prompt: Brings-Them-Back is dead. The channel is clear.
lines.text: Dead. Then nobody knows the way to my tree but me. I did not ask for his death, and I will not call it a pity. Every runaway he turned back was a head-price to him, and I would have been one more. I will go when you have gone from the bank. I have been watched for eleven years, and I will not be watched leaving. Take a word to Never-Sold: the leaf can stay in its box and rot. I am going home, and nothing written on this farm will reach me.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.estate-steward
lines.prompt: Who are you?
lines.text: I am Hulm-Tei, keeper of the count for the Tulm-Varo, who hold this farm. The count is the written account of what each hand on this farm owes. My mistress, who winters in Gideon, far from here, leaves it to me. I was hatched owing on this ground. A debt came with my egg, and the work that pays a debt is called an Owing. Every line I write on a hand's leaf, the page that holds the debt, is true. Forty people eat because the boats go out, and the hands are the ones who row them. When the count is short at the reckoning, when the season's count is closed, the shortage is written on me. So I am hard about a line, and I will not be shamed for it. The keeper before me wrote smaller than I do, and more exactly. You will see it in the first lines of the oldest leaves in the count-box. I keep by the count-box, on the farm by the cattle, because the box is mine to keep.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.estate-steward
lines.prompt: Take the first price and strike her leaf. You have carried worse. (Persuade) (100 gold)
lines.text: I have carried worse than a boat-hand. I have carried it since I was hatched, and I am still on my feet. Then I will take the hundred, and I will strike her leaf with my own hand. Every line on it was true, and I strike it all the same. The eleven years I write onto my own leaf, with my eyes open. Hear what that costs, so that you do not think it nothing. Whatever any leaf is short at the reckoning is written onto the keeper's own, and I am the keeper. If my leaf were ever lost, the hands would share it between them, and I will keep mine where it is. You argued it fairly, and I do not say that often. Go and tell her on the channel bank.

lines.prompt: Who are you?
lines.text: I am Brings-Them-Back. I fetch runaways for the Tulm-Varo, who hold the farm south of here, and for each one I bring home they pay me a head-price, which is a fee for every head. It is 150 gold. Every hand on that farm has a home tree, the Hist their tribe was hatched under, and I alone know the way to each one. A runaway who gets past me can never walk home. I call fetching the kind part of this trade. The Tulm-Varo punish the hands left behind when one runs. The runaway I bring back they treat more kindly, and I would sooner bring one home than watch the others pay for it. I stand where the channel runs on north of the bank, and I keep to it. Rows-For-Another, on the bank just south of here, can tell you what I am to her.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose.estate-fetcher
lines.prompt: Look the other way when Rows-For-Another goes. (Persuade)
lines.text: I have fetched her back twice already, in my head, on nights I could not sleep. I never meant to, either time. You have given me a reason I can carry. I will be looking at the water when she goes, and a man cannot fetch what he does not see. Hear what I keep. I still know the way to her tree, and no word of yours takes it out of me. I look away. I do not lead her home. Go to her, and be quick, before I think better of it.

I do not want to bury you, and I do not want to be buried.

lines: The market's cooking fire? It is north-east of here, a short way. Go on, I have boats to watch.
You are back, my friend. The water is quiet, so stay a while and talk.
Speak. I have boats to watch.
This is Black Rose. The south landing's dock is just south of here. A boat lies just south-south-east. I know her hull.
In the Second Era, word went round the coast that Black Rose had fallen and was gone. It was not. It is still here. I watch its landing.
I am Sakeeth. I watch the south landing for boats that do not pay. I grew up hauling nets on these docks. I joined the guard to be issued boots.
Holds-Fast is the guard on the path above the south docks. He is usually just east-north-east of here. I would trust him in a real fight.
The jail. Walk north-east a short way. It is there.
Haven. Walk south-east a short way, round the cliffs, to the boat on its rack. Then walk south-west a short way, past the stone tower. Haven is there.
It is you. Stand by me a while, my friend. It is quiet here and I am glad of the company.
Stop there. State your business. Let me see what you carry.
The tower is a short way north-north-west of here. Ahkeeh smokes fish in this town. The fish is the best thing in Black Rose. I stand at the edge of Black Rose and count who comes by.
People say many go into Black Rose and few ever leave. Old prison staff, freed prisoners, deserters and runaways all came here and stayed. I have counted a good many of them in at the edge of town.
The dead lie on the road toward Haven. They are Imperials, with an elf among them. The people of Black Rose have not gone to bury them.
I am Tzeel-Vaa, guard where Black Rose ends. I have stood here longer than the two beside me have been alive. My father guarded this same post for the same pay.
Quintel is the other guard at this gate, grandson of an Imperial jailer. He is usually just north-north-east of here. He is too soft for the work.
The cooking fire by the docks? Walk east a short way, and the fire is there. I charge no toll for directions.
You again. Come, stand a while, my friend. For you there is no questioning at this post. I have said that to very few.
I hold this post at the edge of Black Rose. Keep your hands where I can see them.
This is the edge of Black Rose.

Around Black Rose, an owing is taken at a crossing for damage to the way. The debtor works it off on the water. I did that myself once, so I know the sum of it better than most. Now I am the one who stands guard. I will not apologise for the post.

I am Counts-The-Tolls, guard at this post. I was a debtor once, working off an owing on the water. I took this post as the way out. I know how that sounds, but the post is paid work and the water was not.
Tzeel-Vaa is the oldest of the three guards at this post. He is usually just south-south-east of here. He watches my hands at every cart. He should have retired years ago. Speak to him if you must.
Black Rose Jail, traveller? It lies north-east of here, a short walk. Go that way and you will come to it.
Ah, it is you. Forgive me if I stand stiffly. It is how I was taught. I am glad to see you at my post again.
Pardon me, traveller. This is the edge of Black Rose. State your business. I will help if I am able.
This is Black Rose, traveller. The tower stands a short way north-north-west of here.
The people of Black Rose once sent an envoy to the Imperial court. Emperor Pelagius answered him in grunts and squeaks. I do not enjoy telling it, traveller.

I am Quintel, a guard at the edge of Black Rose. I carry the name of the Imperial jailer who raised my grandmother. I answer to no other. My family has worn a uniform in Black Rose for three generations.
Ahkeeh, the fish smoker, keeps the fire at the edge of the town, just north-west of here.
Black Rose Jail. Go north-east a short way, until the statue with the sword is on your left. Then north, just a little further. The jail stands there.
I know your step now. Stand with me a while, if you wish.
Speak quietly here. I keep this stone bird as a shrine. I do not know you yet.
The stone bird is just south-south-west of here. Go to it slowly. Do not climb on it.
The first city here belonged to the Lilmothiit, the fox-folk. Every one of them died of a fever, long before Argonians claimed this place.
I guard the stone bird. The other guards did not want the post, so I asked for it. The bird is older than this town. I keep it as a shrine.
Mireel is a guard on the path above the south docks. You will usually find Mireel a short way south-east of here. Do not expect much from the guards at the docks.
The longboat? Go along the boards east a short way. The longboat is there.
Sunned and warm? I am glad it is you. I have nothing to report today. Ask me what you like.
Halt. State your business here. I was told to ask every stranger, so I am asking you.
I keep watch here, above the dock. There is a cooking fire just south-east of here, and the dock is just south.
When the fever came to Murkmire, the last of the Lilmothiit fled inland toward Black Rose. What became of them is not known. Have you seen any of them on the road?
I am Okaw-Sei, guard at the dock. I keep watch here, above it. I was told to watch for anything unusual. I am newly hatched to the guard, but I mean to serve it well.
Teeda-Wan, the guard at the market, is the best fighter on the docks. You will usually find Teeda-Wan just east-south-east of here.
The cooking fire? Walk south a short way, and you will find it.
Ah, it is you. I am glad of it. Stand by me a while, it is quiet here.
You again. Good. Stay here with me and ask what you like.
Hm. What do you want? Be quick about it.
Mind where you walk, stranger. I am watching where you walk.
This is below the jail. You will find a house just to the south-east.
There is a house just south-east of us. I keep watch near it.
Hm. I know little of Black Marsh, but I know the Rose. Its families are three generations deep. A newcomer owes the prison-born for shelter. The ledger is kept by people who were born owing.
The Rose has families three generations deep. If you are new there, you owe the prison-born for your shelter. The ledger is kept by those who were born owing.
Xuth-Ma. I keep watch below the jail. Dredges-The-Silt is usually near me.
I am a guard below the jail. I do not like the jail. I will not say why.
Dredges-The-Silt is a dredger. I know no better company. You will usually find the dredger just north-west of here.
You want Dredges-The-Silt, the dredger. Look just north-west of here.
The cooking fire? Go south a short way. You cannot miss it.
Still watching that jail, as you see. It is good to talk to someone I trust. I am still waiting for the day it is emptied.
What do you want? I am watching below the jail. Keep your hands where I can see them.
The house is just south-west of here. Go and look at it yourself.
The families who hold the Rose say it is their home, not a prison. They take it badly when outsiders call it one. I call it a jail. I do not care who hears me.
I am Wazei. I keep watch here. My captain has put me where he can see me, because I have been warned twice for wanting a fight with the keepers up there.
Ruh-Jaal is the guard nearest the jail. You will usually find him just west-north-west of here. Do not expect much of him. He is a coward.
Walk just south until you reach the boat on its rack. Then just south-west, and the cooking fire is there. Keep your voice low about who asked.
Come closer, my friend. Keep your voice down. I hear more on this dock than any other guard. For you I will share it.
Keep your voice low. I do not know your face. I like to know every face on this dock.
You are new here. Who have you been speaking to since you arrived?
Quietly now, though everyone knows it. The dock is just south-south-west of here. A boat lies the same way, just as near.
Quietly now. Ask Quintel about the Imperial court. That is his tale, but I would like to know who else asks him for it.
Ask Tzeel-Vaa about the Haven road. I hear everything said on this dock, not what is said elsewhere. I would like to know what he says.
I am Tuh-Weem. I guard this dock. Everything said on it reaches my ears. I am rarely wrong about what I hear.
Mends-The-Hulls mends boats at the north-east dock. She is usually just north-east of here. I think she is courting someone. Ask her yourself.
The longboat? Walk south-east a short way and you will reach it. Mind your boots.
I have time to talk. Stand by me if you like.
Mind where you put your boots.
There is a house just south-east of here. That is all I would point out.
Ask Counts-The-Tolls about crossings and the owing set there. He has forgotten where he came from, so ask him plainly. I have worked mine off for nine seasons.
I am Dredges-The-Silt. I am a dredger. It is owing work. It has taken me nine seasons so far.
Xuth-Ma is the guard on the road to the jail. You will usually find him just south-east of here. He is a good man. He is the one who listens to me.
The cooking fire? Go south, a short way. The fire is there.
Keep your voice low, and stand by me a while. I will not mind the company.
Move along, if you please. I am on watch.
The statue with the sword is just north-west of here, and the jail is just beside the statue. I would not look at the statue for long.
Ask Wazei about what the families call the Rose. I would rather not say it myself. He is a danger to us all, so keep your voice low when you ask.
I am a guard. I stand nearest the jail and keep my post. That is all there is to say.
Pays-In-Reeds is a reed-weaver. She is kind. You will usually find her just north-north-west of here, working off her owing in mats. Ask her, not me.
Black Rose Jail? You can see it from here. It is just south-west. Do not wander off.
The north district is quiet today. I am glad of it. Stay as long as you like.
Speak softly. This is where the families live.
This is the north district, where the families live. I know every child in it by name. The inn is just north-north-west of here.
Ask Sakeeth about the Second Era tale that this town was gone. I guard the north district and leave tales to others.
I am Shaleem. I guard the north district, so mind how you behave in it.
Talks-To-Water is a boat captain in the north district. You will usually find her just east-south-east of here. She should take more care with her boat.
The cooking fire? Everyone knows that. Walk south a short way past the house and you will be standing at it. I could find it with my eyes shut.
I have been watching the water for boats all day! Do you want to hear what I have noticed?
You are new here, are you not? I notice everyone new. Where did you come from? Did you come by boat?
This is the north district. I know all of it. The house is just east-north-east of here. Nobody knows this place better than me.
I am Zeeki. I am the cleverest child in the north district. Ask anyone. One day I will captain a boat of my own.
Talks-To-Water, the boat captain? That is the best captain there is. You will usually find the captain just west-south-west of here. One day I will have a place on that boat.
The cooking fire? A sweet first. Go south-east a short way. You will see the fire.
Did you bring a sweet? I have heard things at the jail, and I will tell you them.
Who are you? Stay where I can see you. Have you got a sweet?
The statue with the sword is just south of here. The tower is just north-north-west. I like sweets better than talking.
I am Skink. I play by the statue, where the other children do not come. I have no family. I hear things at the jail. I tell them for a sweet.
Pays-In-Reeds is nice. She weaves reeds into mats to work off what she owes. She is usually just east-south-east of here.
The cooking fire by the docks? Listen, water, a stranger wants to walk. Go just south-east until you reach the house. Then go south a short way, and the cooking fire is there.
I told the water you would return. Come, sit by it and tell me what you have seen.
You have the look of someone who does not know the water. What do you want?
Quiet, little ones, we have a guest. The house is just south-south-east of here. I keep my boat at the north shore.
Long ago the bandit king Red Bramman ruled this country. He raided Topal Bay from here. The First Empire hunted him for years.

Hush, water. You ask for news, stranger. In the Chainbreakers' house, in the north district, Never-Sold has saved coin to buy a woman free of her Owing at the estate north of Blackrose. Never-Sold is asking for a hand with it.
I am Talks-To-Water. I captain a boat from the north shore. Yes, I talk to the water. My crew is used to it.
Zeeki, the child of the north district, is usually just east-north-east of here. That one should be a sailor. I have said so.
The cooking fire? Go just south, until the longboat is on your left. Then along the boards, just west. The fire is there.
If you have a boat that leaks, bring it to me and I will patch it today.
You are welcome here. Mind your feet, the ground is wet. What needs mending?
What do you want?
Speak quickly.
My house is just north-east of here. The dock is just east-north-east, where the small boats tie up.
My house is just north-east of here. The dock is just east-north-east.
If you want something to do, Never-Sold needs a hand. The money is ready to buy a woman out of her Owing on the estate north of Blackrose. Ask at the Chainbreakers' house in the north district.
I am Mends-The-Hulls. I patch the small boats at the north-east dock, cheap and fast. My mother taught me the trade. She learned it working off an owing.
I mend hulls. Pitch-Pot says my work is careless, but Pitch-Pot is slow and expensive. My patches hold.
Tuh-Weem is the guard at the north-east boat dock. He is usually just south-west of here. He should mind his own dock.
You want Tuh-Weem, the guard at the north-east boat dock. As a rule he is just south-west of here. Go and ask him.
Black Rose Jail is a short way to the north-west of here. Eat before you go.
There you are, my friend. Sit down and eat. You look thin to me.
If you want food, say so. If you do not, I have a fire to watch.
This is Black Rose. My cooking fire is just north-west of here, and the dock is just north-north-east. You have not eaten today, I think.
Ask Tzeel-Vaa about who goes into Black Rose and who stays. I came on a prison barge as its cook, and I never got back on it. Have you eaten?
I am Weeska. I cook at the fire and feed the dock hands. Sit, or move along.
Lux Ha, the net-mender, is usually just south-south-west of here. Lux Ha works too hard. I doubt that one has eaten.
The longboat? Just east of here, in plain sight. You cannot miss it.
Look at what the boats brought in today. If you have something to sell, I will give you a fair price.
Stranger. Buying or selling? I deal in both.
You want something. Say what it is, or show me what you carry.
The market is where the trade is. The cooking fire is just west-north-west of me, and the dock is just north-north-east.
I am Nuxi-Ra. I sell odds and ends here, whatever the boats bring in. I buy from every crew and I do not ask where a thing came from.
Nuxi-Ra. I trade here at the market.
I buy and I sell. I trade at the market, by the cooking fire. My stock is whatever the boats bring in. Show me what you have and I will name a price.
Rows-Against-It captains a boat from the market dock, and is usually just south-south-west of here. Of all the captains, that is the one who pays on time.
Follow the boards north-east a short way, and you will find the longboat.
Calm water today, and a fare I know. My boat is yours if you need her.
If you want a crossing, say where.
My boat is just south of here. The dock is just south-east, so mind your feet.
Ask Okaw-Sei about the last of the Lilmothiit. I carry fares, not old stories. If you want a crossing, say where.
I am Rows-Against-It. I run this boat from the market dock to wherever a fare will go. I paid off my owing on the water and kept the boat. No crossing-keeper gives me orders now.
Weeska cooks at the market fire. She is usually just north-east of here.
The jail. North, a short way. Black Rose Jail is there.
You again, my friend. Good. Stand by the fire and watch the market with me.
Show me your hands. Then say what you want.
Yes. What do you want?
This is the market. The cooking fire is just south of here. So is the dock. Keep the peace and you will have no trouble from me.
Ask Xuth-Ma about the families of the Rose. He talks of it. I do not.
Teeda-Wan. I keep the peace at this market. That is all.
Lux Ha works the nets on the market dock. Usually just east-south-east of here. Lux Ha should be paid more.
The longboat. Yes. Walk south-east a short way, until you reach the house on your left. Then walk south a short way more. The longboat is there.
Hm. Stand with me a while. I am in no hurry. I am glad it is you.
You wish to speak with me? Then speak. I am Iron-Jaw. I guard the north district.
Hm. There is the inn, just there, just north-north-west of where we stand.
Hm. Ask Quintel about Emperor Pelagius. I would like to read his tale in a book one day.
I am Iron-Jaw. A cudgel struck my face in my first year. The name stayed with me. I have stood in the north district ever since. I can read well.
Shaleem is the person you want. Shaleem is a guard in the north district. He is the best guard in the town. You will usually find Shaleem just south-south-east of here.
The cooking fire? South, a fair way past Black Rose. It is there.
Come and stand with me by the boats a while. I could use the company.
I do not know you. Why are you here by the boats?
You are a stranger here. Keep clear of the boats.
A boat lies just north-north-west of here. A rowing boat lies just north.
Black Rose and Lilmoth have been rivals for as long as anyone has kept count. I am a guard, not a teller of old tales.
I am Raxa-Tum. I guard the north edge of Black Rose, where the boats lie. I was a fisher myself once.
Okeemu is the best fisher in town. Okeemu stands just south-west of here, at the north edge of Black Rose.
The jail. Walk south-west a short way. Black Rose Jail is there.
Here you are. I keep watch, as ever. Speak if you wish.
State your business here.
Halt. Say what you want. I am on watch.
This is the north edge of Black Rose. A boat lies just east-south-east.
I keep watch here, at the north edge of Black Rose. There is a boat just east-south-east of where we stand.

In Empress Morihatha's day the people of Black Rose raised an army against the Empire. Her battlemage Welloc broke it with a spell, not with soldiers. In the town, nobody has trusted a battlemage since.
I am Watches-The-Road. I guard the north edge of town. I report every lapse I see. That includes the lapses of other guards.
I am a guard. I watch the north edge and I report what I find.
Raxa-Tum guards the north of Black Rose. You will find him just north-north-west of here, most hours. He idles on duty. He should be dismissed.
The cooking fire? Walk south a fair way, past the house. You will find it there.
Sit by me a while.
I am a fisher. Please speak softly.
This is the north edge of Black Rose. My boat is just north-north-east of here.
Ask Keeps-The-Stone about the Lilmothiit. I know the water and the fish. That is enough for me.
I am Okeemu. I keep my boat at the north edge of Black Rose with my family. It is the oldest boat here.
Heshra the fishwife lives up in the north of the town. She keeps just west of here.

Walk south-east just until you reach Black Rose on your left. Then walk south a short way until you reach the statue on your left. Walk south-east just until you reach the house on your left, then south a short way more. The longboat is there.
For you I will not haggle. Come closer and look at the catch.
What do you want? If you are buying, say what you want and what you will pay.
This is the north edge of Black Rose. The house is just south-south-west of here.
I am Heshra. I gut and sell Okeemu's catch here. I run my family. I watch the prices. A buyer does not bargain with me twice.
Okeemu is usually just east of here. Okeemu is too soft to ask what a catch is worth, so I do the selling.
Go south, past the house. It is a fair way. The cooking fire is there.
It is you, my friend. I practised with my stick today. Nobody laughed.
Oh. Hello. I should be helping my parents, so I cannot talk for long.
I do not know you. What do you want?
The boat is just there, north-north-east of here. You can see it.
I am Pip. Okeemu and Heshra are my parents. I help them with the nets. I am going to be a guard. I practise with a stick.
I watch the guards. Raxa-Tum, the guard at the north edge of Black Rose, is usually just north-east of here. Raxa-Tum is the best guard.
Go north a short way. Black Rose Jail is there.
You again, my friend. Good. The path is quiet, so stay a while.
Keep your hand clear of your weapon. Then say what you want.
The dock is just east-south-east of here. You will see a rowing boat just south-east.
Ask Watches-The-Road about the old rising against the Empire. I guard a path. I do not tell tales.
They call me Holds-Fast. I was the last one standing in a brawl on the docks. The name stayed. I guard the south path. I would rather be feared than liked.
Ten-Coins guards between the south docks and the market. He is usually just north-north-east of here. He will hang one day.
The cooking fire? It is just east of here, in plain sight. Walk straight towards it.
At last I know your name. Stand easy. I do not say that to many.
I do not know you. State your name and your business. Spell the name if it is unusual.
This is Black Rose. The dock is just south-east of here.
Ask Raxa-Tum about Black Rose and Lilmoth. I know Lilmoth. It is a midden.
I am Mireel. I came to Black Rose from Lilmoth and stayed. The guard took me because I can read. I keep the duty rolls for the south docks.
Holds-Fast is usually just south-south-east of here, on this same path. He is a brute, but a useful one.
Black Rose Jail? Walk north a short way, and it is there. I give this way free.
Ah, there you are. Stand with me a while. Today I will name you no price.
Keep your purse close, stranger. Then we will get on well.
You want something from me? Most things here have a price. Mine is always fair.
This is Black Rose. The house is just north-east of here. The market's cooking fire is just east of here.
Ask Xuth-Ma about the Rose and its families. He gives that away for nothing. I give nothing away.
I am Ten-Coins. The name is the price of looking away. Everyone knows it at the docks. I call it a fee, and I call it a fair one.
Okaw-Sei is a guard like me, on the dock walk below the market. You will usually find him just east-south-east of here.
The cooking fire is just south-south-west of here, in plain sight. Walk straight to it.
The dock is quiet. You may stand with me, if you wish.
This dock is watched. Say who you are and why you are here.
I stand on the east dock of Black Rose. There is a house just north-west of me, and a boat just south-east. I keep watch between them.
Ask Watches-The-Road about the town's old war with the Empire. A deserter taught me the sword, not the town's history.
I am Corvane, guard of the east dock and of the big ship moored past it. I took my name from a deserter who taught me the sword. We came to Black Rose together. I stayed after he left.
Pitch-Pot seals the boats at this dock. He works harder than anyone on the docks. You will usually find him just east-south-east of me.
The jail? Walk north-west a short way, and Black Rose Jail is there. Mind your feet as you go!
I smell of pitch, I know, but I am glad to see you! Come close.
Mind your feet. You will smell me before you see me.
Stand back, I smell of pitch. What do you want?
I seal hulls here, so I can tell you about boats. The longboat is just east-south-east of here. A boat lies just south-east.
Ask Sakeeth about the old talk that Black Rose had fallen! I know tar, leaks and rot. She knows the rest.
They call me Pitch-Pot. I got the name as a hatchling, when I fell into the pot. I have smelled of tar ever since.
Corvane is the guard on the east dock. He is a good sort. He is usually just west-north-west of here.
The cooking fire? Go south, a short way. It is there.
The next mat can wait. Sit by me a while.
Mind your step.
I live in the house just north of here, by the jail.
Ask Counts-The-Tolls about the crossing and its owings. I pay mine in mats. It is the ledger I mind, not the work.

Never-Sold has put money aside to buy a woman out of her Owing on the estate north of Blackrose. She is looking for someone to lend a hand. I know what an Owing weighs. Look for Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house, in the north district.
I am Pays-In-Reeds. I weave mats and baskets from marsh reed. I pay my owing in mats. I am working toward my last mat.
Skink is the child who plays by the jail's statue. You will find that child just west-north-west of here. That child should be in a home, not out by a jail.
Black Rose Jail? It is a short way north-west of here. Go that way and you will reach it.
My hands will keep working, but I am glad of the company. Sit a while.
Yes? Say what you want.
This is Black Rose, the market dock. The cooking fire is just west-south-west of here. A boat lies just south-south-west.
Ask Raxa-Tum about Lilmoth. I was born here and have never left, so I can tell you nothing of it.
I am Lux Ha. I mend the nets that come off the market boats. There is always more to mend. I was born in Black Rose and have never left it.
You will usually find Nuxi-Ra, the street vendor at the market, just north of here.
Walk south-west a short way, until the longboat is on your left. Then go along the boards, just west. The cooking fire is there.
Few people come out this far. You are always welcome, my friend. Sit by the water.
Yes? Say what you want.
You are on my dock. Speak, then.
The dock is just south-east of here. My house is just north.
Ask Keeps-The-Stone about the fox-folk. It is not mine to tell. I live at the edge for the quiet.
Three people are shut in the stone house just west of my dock. Third-Born Tsaxi of the Rose keeps them, and he does not like faces at its door.
I am Ree-Shaal. I fish from this dock and live in the house behind it.
I moved out to the edge to be away from the town. I like the quiet. Visitors spoil it.
Sleeps-Standing, the guard at the far east dock, is usually just south-east of here. Go and talk to him.
The cooking fire? Climb west a short way, until the longboat is on your left. Then go along the boards just west. The cooking fire is there.
Hnn. Come, stand with me. Nothing is happening here, and I like it better with you.
Hnn. Yes? Speak. I am listening.
Hm. What is it? Say it plainly.
The dock is just east-south-east of here. The house is just west-south-west. There is not much else to see. I prefer it that way.
Ask Talks-To-Water about Red Bramman. I only stand a post, and I would sooner sleep.
Hnn. The Rose's heirs keep three of their held in the stone house west-north-west of here. Third-Born Tsaxi stands over them. It is their business, so long as nobody bleeds in my town.
I am Sleeps-Standing. I guard the dock at the eastern edge of Black Rose, where nothing happens. I have learned to sleep on my feet. I wake quickly when I must.
Ree-Shaal, the fisher at the far east dock? Usually just north-west of here. Ree-Shaal is a sour one. Ree-Shaal complains about me. Hnn.
Follow the boards west a short way, past the longboat. The cooking fire is there.
You are a welcome sight after a day of crates. Sit a moment, if you can.
Yes. What do you want?
The longboat is just west of here. I live in the house just north-east of here.
Ask Tzeel-Vaa about those who come to Black Rose and stay. I came on a ship myself. I have not decided yet if I was wise to stay.
I am Ojeel. I unload the big ship whenever it comes in. I live in the house by its berth. I signed on to a crew once and walked off it here.
Tadpole, the child who plays around the big ships, is usually just south of here. That child should be kept off the ships.
The cooking fire? Go along the boards north-west a short way, past the longboat. Then you are at the fire. It is easy.
Did you see the ship? Is it still there? I kept watch while you were gone.
Who are you? Are you here to see the ships? Did you drop a coin? I will look for it if you did.
This is the east docks. The longboat is just west-north-west of here, in plain sight. The dock is just north-west. I know every board of it.
Tadpole is my name. I play between the big ships and tell the crews I run their errands. One day I will sail on one. Then you will hear of me. What is your name?
Ojeel? He unloads the big ship. He is usually just north of here. He chases me off the ship every time, so do not say I sent you.
Haven? Walk south-east a short way, until you reach the stone tower. Then walk south-west a short way. Haven is there.
The cooking fire? Walk east a fair way. You will find it there.
The next fish will not be long, so sit by the fire.
Come near the fire and tell me what you need.
The fire is lit. Say what you want.
You are standing in my smoke. Speak, or buy something.
My cooking fire is just west-south-west of here, at the edge of Black Rose. The tower is just north of here.
Ask Talks-To-Water about the old bandit king. I know fish and smoke. That tale takes longer than a fish.
For news of the road toward Haven, ask Tzeel-Vaa. He is the only honest guard at the town's edge, so he will tell it straight.

I am Ahkeeh. I smoke fish over this fire at the edge of Black Rose. I sell it to the guards and to anyone who stops. I was born on a boat and came ashore when it sank. I have not been on the water since.
Tzeel-Vaa is a guard by the town, and I trust him. You will usually find him just south-east of here.

texts.thing.bc01.false-leaf: [In a small, exact hand:] Rows-For-Another. Four nushmeekos for a boat. Worked. Struck.

take: I liked this. The setup was clear: Owings, the Hist and greying, the Chainbreakers. The job gave me three routes with different costs, and none was clean. I failed the persuasion on Hulm-Tei, so I picked the box unseen. Under her leaf I found the keeper's own leaf, which showed that freeing Rows-For-Another would push her debt onto Hulm-Tei or, in the end, onto the dozen hands who stay. Handing him back his leaf with the first price felt like the least bad route, but the hands lose a season each and will never know why. Never-Sold admitting she knew and kept it from me was a good beat. It also left me unsure whether to trust her. I didn't learn how she knew the shape of a keeper's leaf, and I want to. Rough spots: the "seen/unseen" prompt means I choose whether I'm caught, which is odd. The bystanders (Okeemu, Heshra, Pip) only showed generic menus. Rows-For-Another had nothing to say once she was free, so I never got to see her reaction. I would play on with the Chainbreakers, but my journal is empty now.
answers:
1. I don't think I'm meant to do anything right now. My journal is empty and nothing new started after I talked to Never-Sold. The natural next step would be to go back to her, or to the Chainbreakers generally, and ask for more work. I'd also like to find out how she knew what a keeper's leaf looks like. The game hasn't pointed me at that, so it's my own curiosity, not an objective.

2. I work for Never-Sold and the Chainbreakers, at least informally. She gave me the job of freeing Rows-For-Another, and I did it and reported back. I'm not sure I trust her, since she knew the debt would fall on someone else and let me find that out myself. I stay with her because she is the only person offering me work, and I believe in what the Chainbreakers say they are trying to do.

3. The most confusing moment was the "seen/unseen" prompt on the lockpick and the take actions. It seemed to let me choose whether I got caught, so I wasn't sure what I was actually risking. The second most confusing thing was not knowing, after the leaf was returned, who ended up paying the debt. The hands lose a season each and the game never made that visible to me.

4. I'd tell the writer the central dilemma is good. Three routes, none of them clean, and Never-Sold admitting she knew is a strong moment. Here is what to fix:
   - Give the bystanders something real to say, because Okeemu, Heshra and Pip only showed generic menus.
   - Let Rows-For-Another react once she's free, because that reaction is the payoff of the whole quest.
   - Make the seen/unseen choice a real risk, not a decision the player makes.
   - Give the player a lead or an objective after the ending, so the journal isn't empty.
   - Show the consequences for the hands, so the cost I accepted is felt and not just stated.
